Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

replayr 0.3.3

Bug fixes

  • read_bk2() now reads zip members as UTF-8 (falling back to latin1 only for members that are not valid UTF-8). The previous latin1 tag + enc2utf8() double-encoded (mojibake’d) the Unicode face-button glyphs (Triangle/Square/Circle) that Mednafen-family PSX cores (Nymashock) use in their LogKey, so the PSX-core detection failed and the “X” (Cross) column collided with the SNES X-face button while Triangle/Square/Circle went unmapped. Nymashock PlayStation movies now decode their face buttons correctly (verified against the Octoshock recording of the same game).

  • read_gmv() face buttons were rotated relative to BizHawk .bk2 and the physical Genesis controller. The Gens “SACBRLDU” byte spec labels the three face bits B/C/A, but that labeling does not match BizHawk’s A/B/C; across five games recorded in both formats the primary-action button read gmv-A == bk2-C, gmv-B == bk2-A, gmv-C == bk2-B. The three face bits now map to the universal slot of the physical button they actually are, so a game’s attack/jump/magic decode identically from .gmv and .bk2.

replayr 0.3.2

Bug fixes

  • read_pjm() now handles every PSXjin body layout, not just the one-controller <mask>||0| text line. PSXjin renders each frame as <port1>|<port2>|...|<cmd>|, where a port is a 14-character digital mask optionally trailed by space-padded decimal analog-stick values. One-controller movies leave port 2 empty (the historical 20-byte line); two-controller movies fill it (34-byte line); analog movies are wider (52-byte). The reader locates the body by its |CRLF frame terminator, derives the stride and per-port column offsets from the first frame, and reads each port’s digital mask (analog decimals are ignored); two-controller movies yield a two-player movie. Binary-body movies (no text terminator; 5 bytes/frame at the end of the file) are decoded via the shared DualShock bit layout. This fixes the previously-unreadable Metal Gear Solid, Spyro 1 / 2, Klonoa, Pepsiman, Bishi Bashi and Mega Man X4 movies. One-controller decoding is byte-for-byte unchanged. Regression + synthetic tests added.
  • read_fcm() accepts format version 1 as well as 2. The two versions share this header layout and delta-encoded body (the bump only added savestate metadata); verified on real v1 movies (Dragon’s Lair, Power Blade) whose decoded frame counts and press rates are correct. Test added.
  • read_bk2() no longer aborts on archives whose Header.txt carries a NUL-padded fixed-width field (e.g. BoardName NULL\0\0..., written by some Gambatte-core Game Boy movies such as Kwirk and the 4-in-1 Fun Pak titles). Embedded NULs are stripped before the member is decoded as text. Test added.

Known limitations

  • One rare PSXjin binary variant with per-frame analog records (~9 bytes/frame, e.g. Final Fantasy VIII) is detected and rejected with a clear message rather than silently mis-decoded.

replayr 0.3.1

Bug fixes

  • read_fm2() no longer aborts on .fm2 headers that contain non-UTF-8 bytes – e.g. a Shift-JIS romFilename for a Japanese ROM (忍者龍剣伝…), or an 8-bit subtitle. Previously the first regex to touch such a line raised “unable to translate ‘’ to a wide string”. Offending header lines are now re-decoded as latin1 (the fields that carry these bytes are non-essential metadata); valid UTF-8 lines such as accented author names are left untouched. Regression test added.

replayr 0.3.0

New format

  • Doom .lmp – vanilla Doom 1.9 demo format. New read_lmp() entry point. Adds Doom (the historically most influential FPS) to the input-pattern stylometry corpus. Format: 12-byte header (skill / episode / map / dm / respawn / fast / nomonsters / consoleplayer / playeringame[4]) followed by 4-byte-per-tic-per-active-player ticcmd_t records and a 0x80 end marker. Doom’s analog axes (forwardmove / sidemove / angleturn) and the weapon-select state are surfaced as extra per-frame integer matrices in the header slot; ATTACK and USE buttons map to A and B in the universal-buttons array.
  • read_movie() dispatcher and supported_formats() updated to include .lmp.

Format detection

  • Boom / PrBoom+ / dsda-doom extended-format demos (leading 0xFF, 0xCA, or 0xCB) are detected and rejected with a clear error – support for those is a planned v0.4 follow-up.
  • Sub-vanilla files (first byte outside skill range 1..5) are also rejected with a clear diagnostic message.

replayr 0.1.0

Initial release.

Features

  • Pure-R decoders for eleven emulator movie file formats: .fm2 (FCEUX), .bk2 (BizHawk), .fcm (FCEU), .lsmv (lsnes), .gmv (Gens-rerecording), .vbm (VBA-rerecording), .m64 (Mupen64), .smv (Snes9x-rerecording), .pxm and .pjm (PSXjin), and .dtm (Dolphin GameCube).
  • read_movie() dispatches on file extension; per-format readers (read_fm2(), read_bk2(), etc.) are also exported for callers who already know the format.
  • Every parser returns the same replayr_movie S3 object: a per- frame (n_frames, n_players, n_buttons) logical input array, a per-frame integer commands vector, and a header list. The third array dimension is always indexed against a single 30-slot universal-button layout (universal_buttons() / universal_button_names()).
  • Helpers: n_frames(), n_players(), n_buttons(), player(), press_counts(), plus print and format methods for replayr_movie.
  • Eight bundled fixtures under inst/extdata/, one per smaller format, used by the test suite.
  • Optional analog-stick handling: N64, GameCube, and PSX analog sticks are quantised to eight directions and routed into universal slots 21..28; GameCube C-stick / PSX right stick maps onto the N64-style C-button slots 17..20.

Known limitations

  • .dtm Wii movies are not supported (GameCube only for now).
  • .lsmv controller types other than the SNES standard gamepad (12-char masks; 16-char with the lsnes extension suffix) and the Game Boy / GBC libgambatte gamepad (8-char masks) raise an error.
  • A handful of .pjm files in the wild lack the ||0|\r\n body separator the parser scans for; those files raise an error in both the upstream Python implementation and in replayr.
